newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks slide further on poor Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks slide further on poor Q1 earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended an early slump at midday dealing on Thursday in parallel with a slide on Wall Street and a cool reaction to first quarter company earnings.
"Company earnings reports so far have not been very good on the whole. Normally the market is very active in report season, but there is no interest right now," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 37.91 points, or 0.99 percent, at 3,789.10.
Trading volume was dull at 48.9 million shares traded. "There are few foreign investors in the market," the trader added.
Traders were diappointed by the reduced net earnings posted by blue chips such as Maseca and Alfa.
Corn flour and tortilla company Maseca was down 26 centavos at 7.60 pesos, while industrial conglomerate Alfa declined 45 centavos to 44.50 pesos.
Dealers said Telmex, which accounted for some 10 percent of shares traded at midday, weighed heavily on the market and was down in tandem with its ADRs, dragged down in turn by the Dow Jones.
Telmex L shares were down 16 centavos at 16.52 pesos, while its ADRs were off 1/2 to 42.
"We expect Telmex to post earnings this afternoon, and the market is cautiously optimistic, but the Dow is down, ADRs are down and that drags us down, too," another floor trader said.
